To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
2 cell lines from human head‐and‐necksquamous‐cell carcinomashave been established and characterized, and that these cell lines have retained their differentiated phenotype.
two new human cell lines have been established and that they have retained their original differentiated phenotype.
2 cell lines from human oral SCC have been established, characterized and shown to retain their differentiated phenotype in vitro and in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the establishment and characterization of cell lines of human oral SCC, which are suitable for further in vitro studies of SCC biology and for in vivo studies of tumourigenicity and metastasizing behaviour of SCC.
the establishment of a cell‐line system from human head‐and‐neck SCCs, and the characterization of the basic biological parameters.
the development of cell‐line systems for the study of human oral carcinogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 2 cell types represent human SCC in vitro.
these 2 cell lines are suitable models for in vitro studies of SCC of the head and neck.
these 2 cell lines are derived from human head‐and‐ neck SCC and retain their squamous differentiation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the R105 and T87/rc cell lines are useful models for studies of head‐and‐necks SCCs.
both cell lines are tumorigenic, have a high degree of differentiation and are useful models for the study of human oral SCC.
cell lines of human oral SCC can be established which retain their differentiated phenotype.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cell lines of human oral SCC can be established and characterized in such a way that they retain their differentiated phenotype, and can be used for further research on head‐and‐ neck SCC.
the cell lines retain their differentiated phenotype, and that they may be useful for the study of the biology of SCC.
cell lines of human SCCs retain their squamous differentiation in vitro and in vivo.
